name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
summary: An isolation exercise that builds the lateral deltoids by raising dumbbells out to the sides in the scapular plane.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip.
Engage your core, keep your chest upright, and maintain a soft, fixed bend in your elbows.
steps: Raise both arms out to the sides in the scapular plane (roughly 20 to 30 degrees forward of purely lateral).
Lift until your upper arms are approximately parallel to the floor, leading slightly with your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top without shrugging your shoulders into your neck.
Lower the dumbbells smoothly back to your sides under control.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the weights outward; inhale as you lower them with control.
cues: Pour water from a pitcher at the top.
Lead with the elbows, not the wrists.
Keep shoulders depressed away from your ears.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso or using leg drive to heave the dumbbells upward.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load and keep your torso stationary throughout the movement.

common_faults.fault: Raising the hands significantly higher than the elbows.
common_faults.correction: Focus on lifting your elbows and keep wrists neutral and aligned with the forearms.

common_faults.fault: Excessively shrugging the shoulders upward toward the ears.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades pulled down to maximize tension on the lateral deltoids rather than the upper traps.

precautions: Avoid lifting directly in the frontal plane if you experience shoulder impingement; keep the arms slightly forward in the scapular plane.
